title: Closed-Loop PID Speed & Position Control of a DC Servomotor

content.aim: To design, simulate, and experimentally tune a Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controller for angular velocity tracking and steady-state error elimination in a permanent magnet DC servomotor.
objectives: To obtain the open-loop transfer function and electromechanical time constants of the DC servomotor.
To implement quadrature encoder signal decoding using microcontroller external interrupt channels.
To apply the Ziegler-Nichols tuning method to evaluate rise time, settling time, and percentage overshoot under variable mechanical loads.
apparatus: Permanent Magnet DC Servomotor with built-in 500 PPR optical incremental encoder
STM32F401RE ARM Cortex-M4 Microcontroller Development Board
VNH5019 Dual H-Bridge Motor Driver Module (30A, 24V)
Magnetic hysteresis friction brake load attachment

theory.text: A permanent magnet DC motor behaves as an electromechanical transducer whose armature dynamics are governed by Kirchhoff's voltage law and Newton's second law of rotational motion. The continuous-time PID control law computes an actuation voltage u(t) = Kp * e(t) + Ki * ∫e(τ)dτ + Kd * (de(t)/dt). The proportional term accelerates transient response, the integral term eliminates steady-state offsets caused by friction, and the derivative term provides phase lead damping against transient oscillations.

procedure: Wire the STM32 timer encoder interface pins (TIM3_CH1 and TIM3_CH2) to the quadrature optical encoder outputs A and B.
Connect the PWM output pin (TIM1_CH1 at 20 kHz) and direction GPIO pins to the VNH5019 H-bridge motor driver.
Supply the driver with 12.0V DC and verify open-loop rotational speed characteristics by stepping PWM duty cycles from 10% to 90%.
Flash the digital PID control algorithm configured with a 1.0 ms sampling loop (Ts = 0.001s).
Set Ki = 0 and Kd = 0, then gradually increase proportional gain Kp until continuous, sustained oscillations (ultimate gain Ku) are observed on the oscilloscope.
Record the critical oscillation period (Tu) and calculate Ziegler-Nichols parameters for P, PI, and PID modes.
Apply a step velocity reference from 0 to 1200 RPM and record step response data into the real-time telemetry buffer.
precautions: Ensure a common ground connection is established between the microcontroller logic and the 12V high-current motor power supply to prevent ground-loop voltage spikes.
Implement a derivative low-pass filter (cutoff frequency N = 100) to prevent high-frequency encoder quantization noise from saturating the H-bridge.
Never exceed the rated stall current limit (3.2A) for more than 5 seconds during locked-rotor torque testing.

content.discussion: The open-loop DC motor exhibited substantial steady-state velocity sag (48.5 RPM offset) when mechanical friction was applied to the rotor. Implementing pure proportional control reduced the rise time to 42.0 ms but introduced 28.4% peak overshoot and failed to remove steady-state error entirely. The addition of the integral accumulator successfully drove the steady-state tracking error to zero, while the derivative damping term suppressed oscillatory ringing, reducing settling time from 210.0 ms down to 64.0 ms.
content.conclusion: The closed-loop PID controller was successfully deployed and tuned on the ARM Cortex-M4 platform. The fine-tuned parameters (Kp = 3.10, Ki = 11.20, Kd = 0.22) achieved optimal damping with a rapid rise time of 26.5 ms and zero steady-state tracking error under rated load.

questions.question: What is 'integral windup' in PID speed control, and how is it mitigated?
questions.answer: Integral windup occurs when large step setpoint errors cause the integral accumulator to sum excessively while the motor driver output is already saturated at 100% duty cycle. It is mitigated using anti-windup clamping algorithms (clamping the integral sum whenever actuator limits are reached).

questions.question: Why is quadrature decoding preferred over single-channel tachometer sensing?
questions.answer: Quadrature decoding uses two 90-degree phase-shifted channels (A and B), which allows the microcontroller to instantly detect bidirectional rotation (clockwise vs counter-clockwise) and quadruple the effective positional resolution via 4X edge counting.

learnings: Mastered low-level hardware timer configuration for optical quadrature encoder decoding on ARM microcontrollers.
Gained practical experience in real-time discrete PID implementation and anti-aliasing filter design for electro-mechanical actuators.
